awd_titl_txt: Conference: Developing Guidance for the Use of Artificial Intelligence in STEM Education Research
awd_abstract_narration:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools are being adopted at an unprecedented rate, offering powerful new capabilities for researchers in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics (STEM) education. While these tools can accelerate discovery, they also present significant challenges such as providing inaccurate or limited information. This project aims to develop guidelines for STEM education researchers so that they can use these novel tools effectively and responsibly. This project addresses a critical gap by bringing together experts from a variety of fields at a conference to develop foundational guidance for the responsible use of AI in STEM education and research. This work serves the national interest by lessening the risk of using AI in STEM education.

The rapid proliferation of Large Language Models (LLMs) and other AI tools in the research workflow has outpaced the development of professional standards for their use. Thus, this project convenes a conference of experts to create guidance for the responsible use of AI within the context of STEM education research. The project centers on expanding the understanding that STEM education researchers have of the complex issues involved with the use of AI and seeks to establish a framework for decision-making. The conference and subsequent activities address two central research questions: (1) what are the opportunities, challenges, and risks pertaining to the use of AI tools in STEM education research? and (2) what ethical issues, including authorship and data privacy, should STEM education researchers consider when using AI tools in their research? The project contributes to the development and dissemination of AI guidelines that will inform and enhance STEM education research.

This award reflects NSF's statutory mission and has been deemed worthy of support through evaluation using the Foundation's intellectual merit and broader impacts review criteria.

por.por_cntn:
Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly changing how science is conducted. However, many researchers studying science, technology, engineering, and math (STEM) education lack the technical background to confidently navigate the ethical, privacy, and practical hazards of using AI—especially when working with human participants and students.

To address this critical gap and advance research integrity (Intellectual Merit), our project team led the creation of a comprehensive report: Guidelines for Responsible Use of AI in STEM Education Research: Protecting Participant Communities and Research Integrity. This foundational document was created by a team of nearly 30 education researchers across various STEM fields. The guidelines enable education researchers without expertise in generative AI to understand issues related to the responsible use of generative AI in the research process.

The guidelines were developed through a collaborative, consensus-building process with experts and stakeholders. Participant feedback validated our approach to gathering this knowledge. One respondent noted that, “the planning and email communications were excellent and so was managing time.” Another reported that, “This process work[ed] well to capture the ideas of a group. I appreciate the multiple rounds of information gathering.”

To ensure this knowledge translates into tangible societal and scientific benefits (Broader Impacts), we created supplementary materials to support the report and help research groups put these concepts into practice. These resources provide immediate, practical safeguards for participant communities and include:

  • A Decision-making Flowchart for Responsible Use of AI in Education Research

  • A Template for an AI Use Log and Policy for Education Researchers

  • Template Participant Consent/Assent Clauses for Using AI in Education Research (for inclusion in Institutional Review Board applications)

  • A checklist of Critical Questions to Consider Before Using AI in Education Research

Over the life of the award, we focused heavily on the broad dissemination of the guidelines and Report across several communities of STEM education researchers. These outreach efforts have contributed to how researchers evaluate the risks and rewards of AI tools.

After participating in one such dissemination workshop, a participant shared that “This opened up some new ideas that I really do need to think about when AI tools are actually being used.” Another expressed the profound impact the project had on their future work, stating: “The exploration of responsible AI use opened up my eyes to the hazards – I had not considered half of the nine areas of concern. I was so focused on the potential benefits for so many aspects of productivity in work-life balance that I neglected to evaluate consequences. This has tremendous implications for my research designs moving forward.”

Ultimately, this project has equipped the STEM education research community with the necessary guidance to protect study participant communities and maintain the highest ethical standards.

Modified by: Monica M McGill
